---
title: "Interface China ↔ CBAM"
subtitle: "Can a carbon price paid in China be deducted under CBAM?"
---

::: {.stand}
Last checked: 13 Oct 2026
:::

## Starting point

Since 2025, three sectors are covered **both** by China's emissions trading scheme **and** by CBAM:

| Sector | China ETS [@mee_2025] | CBAM [@eu_cbam_2023, Annex I] |
|---|:-:|:-:|
| Steel / iron and steel | ✓ | ✓ |
| Cement | ✓ | ✓ |
| Aluminium | ✓ | ✓ |

## What Article 9 of the CBAM Regulation requires

The number of CBAM certificates to be surrendered can be reduced by a carbon price paid in the country of origin — subject to conditions [@eu_cbam_2023, Art. 9]:

1. The carbon price must **actually have been paid** for the declared emissions.
2. **Rebates or other compensation** in the country of origin that lower the price must be deducted.
3. Payment must be **documented**, and the documentation certified by an **independent person** — independent of the declarant and of the authorities of the country of origin.
4. Details (conversion of the annual average price, exchange rate, evidence) are set by the Commission in implementing acts.

## My assessment

::: {.einordnung}
- **Free allocation does not count as payment.** In the first compliance year, 2024, allocation in China matched verified actual emissions [@mee_2025]. For many installations the price effectively paid is therefore likely close to zero — and so is any possible deduction.
- **With the tightening from 2027** [@mee_2025], an actually paid price may arise. The question then becomes how it is evidenced and converted per tonne of product.
- **Evidence is the bottleneck.** Certification by independent third parties creates demand for verification that understands Chinese data and rules — and, on the EU side, for people who can read both systems.

This assessment is not legal advice.
:::
